title: Cohomology of an affine line with an exponential sheaf
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$ and a nontrivial additive character $\Psi:(\mathbf F_p,+)\to\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell^\times$. Let $k$ be a finite or algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$, let $a\in k$, put $K=\bar k$, and let $i\geq0$. Use the adic coefficient category [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category]; $H^i$ means the $i$-th cohomology of its ordinary derived global-section complex. On $\mathbf A^1_k$, let $\mathcal L_{\psi_a}=\mathcal L_{\Psi,ax}$ be the pullback of the prime-field Artin–Schreier sheaf of [sk-def-as], applied with the finite field $\mathbf F_p$ and coefficient ring $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Thus it is the $\Psi$-isotypic summand of the covering $T^p-T=ax$. For finite $k$, the notation is $\psi_a(x)=\psi(ax)$ with $\psi=\Psi\circ\operatorname{Tr}_{k/\mathbf F_p}$; over algebraically closed $k$ the notation denotes this same prime-field sheaf construction, not a field trace from $k$ to $\mathbf F_p$. Then
$$
H^i(\mathbf A^1_K,\mathcal L_{\psi_a})\cong
\begin{cases}\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell,&i=0,\ a=0,\\0,&\text{otherwise.}\end{cases}
$$

proof.text: Work over $K=\bar k$. By [lem-fd-as-cover-affine-line], the cover for the coordinate $x$ is $\pi:\mathbf A^1_{K,y}\to\mathbf A^1_{K,x}$, $x=y^p-y$, with translations $\sigma_b(y)=y+b$ for $b\in\mathbf F_p$; its finite etale torsor property is [lem-fd-as-cover]. Apply [lem-fd-as-characters] to obtain $\pi_*\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell=\bigoplus_\chi\mathcal L_\chi$. With the prime-field definition [sk-def-as], $\mathcal L_{\Psi,x}$ is precisely the summand on which $\sigma_b$ acts by $\Psi(b)$. All these objects descend to a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ containing the $p$-th roots of unity: the defining coefficients $p^{-1}\Psi(-b)$ lie in $\mathcal O_E$, since $p\ne\ell$. Hence the constant lattice and its character projectors give compatible finite free lisse coefficient systems. The finite-etale exchange of [lem-fd-finite-etale-adic-cohomology], applied to the prime-field cover and its pullback to $K$, identifies the pulled-back character summand in [sk-def-as] with this isotypic summand. All schemes in this square are noetherian of finite dimension, and $\ell$ is invertible on them.

source.place: Proof, Artin–Schreier cover and its cohomology

proof.text: Apply [lem-fd-finite-etale-adic-cohomology] with $Y=\mathbf A^1_{K,y}$, $X=\mathbf A^1_{K,x}$ and the constant coefficient system. It gives $H^i(X,\pi_*\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)\cong H^i(Y,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ and identifies the action of every deck translation on both sides. The hypotheses hold: both lines are noetherian and finite-dimensional, $\ell$ is invertible on them, and Step 1 supplies the finite etale map and coefficient system. This comparison uses adic coefficients throughout; the torsion-only statement lem-fd-finite-pushforward-cohomology is not applied directly to rational coefficients.

source.place: Proof, Artin–Schreier cover and its cohomology

proof.text: Finite direct-sum inclusions $j_\chi$ and projections $r_\chi$ satisfy $r_\chi j_{\chi'}=\delta_{\chi\chi'}$ and $\sum_\chi j_\chi r_\chi=1$. Applying the additive cohomology functor preserves these identities, so Step 1 and Step 2 give $\bigoplus_\chi H^i(X,\mathcal L_\chi)\cong H^i(Y,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$. By [lem-fd-affine-line-constant-cohomology] the right side is zero for $i>0$. Each summand is then zero, because its identity factors through that zero group.

source.place: Proof, Artin–Schreier cover and its cohomology

proof.text: In degree zero, [lem-fd-affine-line-constant-cohomology] makes $H^0(Y,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ one-dimensional. The constant global section $1$ is nonzero (its value at $y=0$ is $1$), so it spans this group: every global section is a constant $c$. Pullback of a constant section $c$ by $y\mapsto y+b$ is again $c$, so all translations act as the identity. On the image of $H^0(X,\mathcal L_\Psi)$, however, Step 1 makes $\sigma_b$ multiplication by $\Psi(b)$. Choose $b$ with $\Psi(b)\ne1$. Every vector $v$ in this image satisfies $(\Psi(b)-1)v=0$, and this nonzero scalar is invertible in $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, hence $v=0$. The inclusion is split by $H^0(r_\Psi)$, so $H^0(X,\mathcal L_{\Psi,x})=0$. Together with Step 3 this gives vanishing for the nontrivial coordinate sheaf in every degree.

source.place: Proof, Artin–Schreier cover and its cohomology

proof.text: If $a\ne0$, the maps $m_a(x)=ax$ and $m_{a^{-1}}(x)=a^{-1}x$ are inverse scheme automorphisms of $\mathbf A^1_K$. By the pullback definition [sk-def-as], $\mathcal L_{\Psi,ax}=m_a^*\mathcal L_{\Psi,x}$. More explicitly, substituting $x\mapsto ax$ in $K[x,T]/(T^p-T-x)$ gives $K[x,T]/(T^p-T-ax)$ and leaves every translation $T\mapsto T+b$ unchanged, hence leaves the character projector unchanged. An isomorphism identifies the small sites by $U\mapsto U\times_{m_a}\mathbf A^1_K$ with inverse given by $m_{a^{-1}}$, preserving coverings and the terminal object. It therefore relabels the sheaf categories, their resolutions and global-section complexes; the same relabeling applies to coefficient towers and their rationalizations. Thus $H^i(\mathbf A^1_K,m_a^*F)\cong H^i(\mathbf A^1_K,F)$. Take $F=\mathcal L_{\Psi,x}$ and apply Steps 3–4.

source.place: Proof, Artin–Schreier cover and its cohomology

proof.text: If $a=0$, the cover $T^p-T=0$ splits as $\coprod_{b\in\mathbf F_p}\mathbf A^1_K$, since $T^p-T=\prod_b(T-b)$ and distinct roots differ by a unit. Its pushforward consists of functions on $\mathbf F_p$ with values in the constant coefficient sheaf. The functions satisfying $v(b+c)=\Psi(c)v(b)$ are exactly $v(b)=\Psi(b)v(0)$; evaluation at zero identifies this summand with the constant rank-one sheaf. The finite-etale exchange [lem-fd-finite-etale-adic-cohomology] identifies the zero pullback in [sk-def-as] with the character summand of this split cover. By the isotypic definition this is $\mathcal L_{\Psi,0}$. Now [lem-fd-affine-line-constant-cohomology] gives $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ in degree zero and zero above. Along with Step 5 this is the asserted formula.
